definitions.explanation: Traveling from place to place without a fixed destination or home. Can be romantic (the wandering artist) or negative (homelessness), depending on context.

examples.japanese: {若|わか}い{頃|ころ}、{世界|せかい}を{放浪|ほうろう}した。
examples.english: When I was young, I wandered the world.

examples.japanese: {放浪|ほうろう}の{旅|たび}に{出|で}た{詩人|しじん}がいた。
examples.english: There was a poet who set out on a wandering journey.

examples.japanese: {仕事|しごと}を{辞|や}めて{一年間|いちねんかん}ヨーロッパを{放浪|ほうろう}した{経験|けいけん}が、{人生観|じんせいかん}を{変|か}えた。
examples.english: The experience of quitting my job and wandering Europe for a year changed my outlook on life.

notes:
USAGE:
Carries a literary, romantic quality when describing travel with no fixed plans. In negative contexts, can imply vagrancy or aimlessness. Often used with の to modify nouns: {放浪|ほうろう}の{旅|たび} (wandering journey), {放浪|ほうろう}の{画家|がか} (wandering painter).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {放浪|ほうろう}の{旅|たび}: a wandering journey
- {各地|かくち}を{放浪|ほうろう}する: to wander from place to place
- {放浪|ほうろう}{生活|せいかつ}: a nomadic life
- {放浪|ほうろう}{者|しゃ}: a wanderer, vagrant
